Name: C2C_LINKUP_FAILED
Message: C2C lanes failed to train or link up within the timeout: RX equalization did not converge after its configured attempts, or the link-up test reported one or more datalinks/lanes down.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal SERDES TX/RX lane on the module | FIR taps from the preceding sweep not valid for this rate/FEC mode | Loopback fixture or cable not seated on the station | PHY configuration mismatch for the requested FEC mode

Name: C2C_LOOPBACK_DATA_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH
Message: Bit-by-bit C2C loopback comparison found a data mismatch on at least one datalink/lane.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal SERDES lane corrupting data under load | FEC not correcting at the configured rate for this lane | Loopback lane map does not match the fixture wiring | CSRAM/WDMA data path defect on the module

Name: C2C_LOOPBACK_THROUGHPUT_BELOW_THRESHOLD
Message: The large C2C transfer did not meet its acceptance criteria: measured throughput below the configured percentage of line rate (90% in the 1X suite), or the post-FEC uncorrected error fraction above its limit.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal SERDES lane forcing FEC retransmission/correction | CSRAM PLL not held at the test frequency for the transfer | DMA read arbiter FIFO depth misconfigured for the rate | Loopback fixture insertion loss out of spec

Name: C2C_LANE_MARGIN_BELOW_THRESHOLD
Message: Worst per-lane minimum BER from the eye-diagram sweep exceeded the configured ber_threshold. The SERDES margin spec is not final, so this code is severity 4 (triage) rather than a straight isolate: confirm against the current spec before dispositioning a module.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal SERDES lane (closed eye) on the module | Eye-diagram sweep threshold tighter than the (unfinalized) SERDES spec | PRBS pattern or rate not matched to the station fixture | Loopback fixture insertion loss out of spec

Name: C2C_PRBS_ERROR_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED
Message: The C2C PRBS run completed but the measured pre-FEC bit-error rate exceeded max_pre_fec_ber on at least one lane.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal SERDES TX/RX lane on the module | FIR taps from the preceding sweep not valid for this rate/FEC mode | Loopback fixture or cable not seated on the station

Name: C2C_LINK_STABILITY_FAILED
Message: A C2C lane lost lock in the stability test and went link down. This is a risk for kayak and this should be investigated.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Loss of receiver clock recovery (CDR) mid-way through the test.

Name: DMA_DATA_PATH_FAIL
Message: Host-chip DMA data-path test failure: dma_test_app reported a data verification or March C+ failure on an SRAM region (RopeSram / CentralSram), or failed in a way its output does not attribute to a more specific PCIe/HBM failure mode (fallback for this test).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspected test issue (single chip test timeout took down the station), retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal PCIe or on-chip data path corrupting DMA transfers | Stuck or transition-faulty bits in the target SRAM region | DMA engine / descriptor handling fault

Name: SOHU_FIRMWARE_UPDATE_FAILED
Message: The Sohu application firmware update did not complete: loading or executing the image package raised, the ASIC did not become pingable afterwards, or the ASIC came back without reporting application firmware. For the hot-reload case it also covers the pre-update eligibility outcomes, where nothing was flashed at all — the chip is running a legacy bootloader, is in bootloader mode with no application PLDM endpoint, or the precheck could not read the running versions over RPC/proxy.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Image package rejected by the bootloader (bad signature or layout) | ASIC hung during the jump to application firmware | Mezzanine/VBB comms lost mid-update | Suite ran the hot reload before secure_bootloader and an application firmware were in place | Power sequencing fault during the update

Name: SOHU_FIRMWARE_IMAGE_HASH_MISMATCH
Message: The ASIC booted application firmware after the update, but the running image hash from get_version_info() does not match the hash in the image package that was just staged.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Station staged an image package from a different release | Update silently fell back to a previously flashed image | Image package metadata (version info) does not match its payload | QSPI/bootloader served a stale image

Name: BOOTLOADER_PROGRAMMING_FAILED
Message: Bootloader programming failed (flash program fail or no ping after program).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Verify that the green power indicators on the Sohu module are ON. Verify that both the PCIe cable and power cable are connected correctly and securely. If there is no trouble found, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Bootloader flash programming failed | ASIC did not respond after programming

Name: JTAG_IMAGE_LOAD_VERIFY_FAILED
Message: JTAG image load/verify failed (ICCM verify mismatch).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspected test issue, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: JTAG image load or ICCM verification failed

Name: FIXTURE_FIRMWARE_UPDATE_FAILED
Message: Fixture firmware update failed (golden VBB / retimer): OpenOCD flash, ST-Link adapter, post-flash UART/RPC ready check, or application firmware-hash verification did not succeed.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Reboot Devkit, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Fixture firmware update or verification failed | ST-Link / OpenOCD flash failure on the VBB MCU | VBB UART unavailable or RPC unresponsive after reboot | Flashed image hash does not match the running application

Name: BOARD_DVFS_PROFILE_FAILED
Message: Board DVFS profile detection or application failed.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Profile missing for this board revision | Board ID readback fault

Name: SECURE_BOOT_RECOVERY_UPDATE_TIMEOUT
Message: The PLDM Update Agent did not complete within pldm_update_timeout_s during a secure-boot recovery update - the device is likely not responding over the Sohu UART in recovery mode.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Verify UART cabling and that recovery straps engage; rerun once; preserve logs and route to FW triage
Possible Root Cause: Device not actually in recovery mode (strap sequence ineffective) | Sohu UART unresponsive or wrong port/baudrate | Update stalled mid-transfer

Name: SECURE_BOOT_RECOVERY_UPDATE_FAIL
Message: The VFIO app firmware update through secure-boot recovery mode failed - the recovery strap sequence failed or the PLDM Update Agent reported an update failure (non-zero pldm_ua exit, update rejected by the device). Tooling/deployment gaps are TH-HAR-0003; invalid args are TH-HAR-0002.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Verify UART cabling/seating and rerun recovery-update subset once; then preserve unit + pldm_ua log and verify package vs release; route to FW triage - do NOT keep retrying as device may be mid-update
Possible Root Cause: Device did not enter or hold secure-boot recovery mode (strap/VBB issue) | PLDM package rejected by the device (image/signature mismatch) | Sohu UART communication errors during the update

Name: SOHU_HOT_RELOAD_NOT_ELIGIBLE
Message: The hot reload could not start, so no firmware was written: the chip is running a legacy bootloader rather than secure_bootloader, it is in bootloader mode with no application PLDM endpoint, or the precheck could not read the running versions over RPC/proxy. The suite must run secure-boot recovery or bootstrap before this test case. Distinct from TH-FW-0001, which covers an update that was attempted and failed.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Escalate to Etched with the eligibility outcome and the running image name; nothing was flashed, so do not route the unit to rework or FA.
Possible Root Cause: Suite ran the hot reload before secure_bootloader and an application firmware were in place | An earlier recovery/bootstrap step in the suite failed and was not gated on | PCIe/proxy state left the application PLDM endpoint unreachable

Name: SOHU_FIRMWARE_VERSION_MISMATCH
Message: The running Sohu firmware is not the image the suite requires: application firmware was expected, but the chip reported only a bootloader slot. The inverse (application firmware running when the step did not expect it) is a suite sequencing problem and stays unclassified.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: A preceding firmware-update step did not run or did not complete | The chip reset back into bootloader mode after the update | Suite configuration expects a release the unit was never staged with

Name: HBM_PMBIST_FAILURE
Message: HBM PMBIST failure.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: HBM stack cell or repair-map fault | Marginal HBM interface at speed
Bugs: ETCH-33885: Power Virus failures [was SohuPmbistTestCase failures]

Name: HBM_EYE_MARGIN_BELOW_THRESHOLD
Message: HBM training / eye margin below threshold (tentative).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal HBM channel eye | Threshold still under review (tentative)

Name: HBM_MTC_STRESS_FAILURE
Message: HBM MTC stress test failure.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspected test issue, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: HBM stack fault under stress | Marginal pseudo-channel at speed

Name: HBM_BANDWIDTH_BELOW_THRESHOLD
Message: PCIe-to-HBM read or write throughput did not reach the configured floor.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: HBM channel running below rate after training | Degraded or repaired HBM lanes reducing effective width | Sohu HBM controller or DMA engine underperforming

Name: HBM_LANE_REPAIR_FAILED
Message: Lane repair established that one or more HBM pseudo-channels cannot be repaired within spare coverage. Covers a completed sweep with per-target errors (fail_fast=False), and fail_fast raises that prove unrepairability (exhausted candidate byte pairs, multi-bit / aword / DWORD LFSR unrepairable, or applied repairs still failing verification). Distinct from TH-HBM-0008, which covers an aborted sweep where repairability was never established (RPC / firmware / setup).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: More failing lanes on the pseudo-channel than there are spares | HBM stack or interposer defect beyond lane-repair coverage | Sohu HBM PHY fault on the affected channel

Name: HBM_DEVICE_ID_READ_FAIL
Message: The IEEE 1500 DRAM device ID could not be read from every HBM stack, or the reported stack topology did not match the expected stack count. Covers an unreadable device ID (RPC error, timeout, or unexpected response) as well as a missing channel id or wrong number of stacks in the reported system info.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: HBM stack not responding on its IEEE 1500 port | Stack absent, misassembled, or not trained during bring-up | Sohu HBM controller fault on the affected stack

Name: HBM_LANE_REPAIR_INCOMPLETE
Message: The lane-repair detection sweep did not run to completion, so whether a passing repair exists was never established. Covers unexpected detection abort (RPC / TypeError / firmware reload after clearing persisted repairs) before an unrepairable verdict. Distinct from TH-HBM-0006, which covers proven unrepairability (exhausted candidates, multi-bit / aword / DWORD LFSR unrepairable, or repairs that still fail verification).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Escalate to Etched with the detection exception and the partial repair map; repairability is unknown rather than failed, so do not route the unit to FA.
Possible Root Cause: Detection RPC or SPI-flash access failed partway through the sweep | Firmware reload after clearing persisted repairs did not come back | Repair-map merge hit a conflicting or out-of-range persisted entry

Name: HBM_NOT_TRAINED_FOR_REQUIRED_SPEED
Message: The chip does not carry HBM DCDL training covering every pseudo-channel of every HBM at the data rate the suite requires, or is running a different rate. Also covers a Flash init-config overlay that does not decode at all, which means no persisted training exists. Firmware refuses an untrained module its trained production point, and nothing else in the suite fails on such a chip, so without this check an untrained socket ships. The emitting case only reads the persisted records and the running speed bin; it changes nothing on the chip.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Confirm the unit's board/chip swap history since its last HBM training run. Request an HBM training run at the required data rate for the HBMs named by the untrained bitmask, then rerun this suite. If training completes and the socket still reports untrained HBMs, escalate to Etched with the suite logs.
Possible Root Cause: HBM training was never run on this unit at the required data rate | Training ran at a different rate (e.g. a DVT rate) than the one required | Training covered only some HBMs or some pseudo-channels of an HBM | A board or chip swap after training left the socket with no records | The Flash init-config overlay was erased or is corrupt

Name: MEZZANINE_CPLD_ACCESS_WRITE_FAILED
Message: Mezz/eval CPLD register access or write failure.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Verify that the green power indicators on the Sohu module are ON. Verify that both the PCIe cable and power cable are connected correctly and securely. If there is no trouble found, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Mezzanine or eval-board CPLD register access failed | Devkit cannot communicate with the Sohu module, it is likely that the bootloader is not running because the PV1 is not powering on

Name: UNEXPECTED_MEZZANINE_I2C_ALERT
Message: Unexpected mezzanine I2C alert asserted.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspected test issue, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Unexpected mezzanine I2C alert state

Name: EXPECTED_MEZZANINE_I2C_ALERT_NOT_OBSERVED
Message: Expected mezzanine I2C alert was not observed.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspected test issue, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Expected mezzanine I2C alert state was not reported

Name: PCIE_LINK_STATE_MISMATCH
Message: PCIe link state mismatch: the Sohu endpoint link is not L0 / Gen5 / x16.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspect PCIe cable not fully seated into PV1 board, reseat the cable and retest once.
Possible Root Cause: PCIe link degraded or retrained at a lower speed/width | Marginal PCIe channel or connector seating

Name: PCIE_AER_ERRORS_DETECTED
Message: PCIe AER errors detected (correctable or uncorrectable).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspect PCIe cable not fully seated into PV1 board, reseat the cable and retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal PCIe channel producing correctable errors | Connector contamination or seating
Bugs: ETCH-34150: Power Virus failures [was SohuPcieAerCheckTestCase failures]

Name: PCIE_CSRAM_DMA_THROUGHPUT_BELOW_THRESHOLD
Message: PCIe->CSRAM DMA throughput below the qualified floor (suite-configured; 50 GB/s for the 1X module suite). Emitted by SohuDmaTestCase when its CentralSram throughput check fails in the active DMA flow.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: PCIe link degraded (lane width / speed below Gen5 x16) | Marginal PCIe channel forcing correctable-error retries | DMA engine or arbitration issue limiting transfer rate

Name: PCIE_HBM_DMA_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH
Message: PCIe->HBM DMA data integrity mismatch: dma_test_app read back data from an HBM region (EastHbm / WestHbm) that does not match the written random / bit-inverse pattern.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: HBM stack or pseudo-channel data fault | Marginal PCIe or on-chip path corrupting transfers to HBM | DMA addressing fault targeting the wrong block/offset

Name: PCIE_HBM_DMA_THROUGHPUT_BELOW_THRESHOLD
Message: PCIe->HBM DMA throughput below the qualified floor (suite-configured; 16 GB/s for the 1X module suite) on EastHbm / WestHbm transfers in dma_test_app.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: PCIe link degraded (lane width / speed below Gen5 x16) | HBM stack or controller limiting sustained bandwidth | DMA engine or arbitration issue limiting transfer rate

Name: PCIE_SPEED_CHANGE_FAILED
Message: PCIe speed change failed (Gen5<->Gen1 transition did not complete).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspect PCIe cable not fully seated into PV1 board, reseat the cable and retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Link training failure at the target rate | Marginal PCIe channel at Gen5

Name: PCIE_LANE_MARGIN_BELOW_THRESHOLD
Message: PCIe lane margin below threshold (EH>25mV EW>0.2UI, tentative).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspect PCIe cable not fully seated into PV1 board, reseat the cable and retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal PCIe channel on one or more lanes | Threshold still under review (tentative)

Name: SOHU_ENDPOINT_NOT_ENUMERATED
Message: Sohu endpoint not enumerated (absent from PCIe tree / RPC proxy).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Suspect PCIe cable not fully seated into PV1 board, reseat the cable and retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Sohu endpoint is absent from the PCIe tree or RPC proxy
Bugs: ETCH-35872: Chips not enumerated by RPC proxy

Name: POWER_TELEMETRY_UNAVAILABLE
Message: Power telemetry unavailable (VBB / VRM / VM sensor RPC / collectors not responding, or expected VM sensors missing from the reading response).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: VBB comms failure on the golden VBB fixture | Sohu DVFS RPC failure while reading VM sensors | Telemetry collector not running

Name: POWER_DATA_OUT_OF_RANGE
Message: Power data out of the qualified range, or CPLD reports an active VRM FSM fault on the mezzanine.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Module power delivery out of qualified envelope | Rail fault under load | Mezzanine CPLD VRM sequencing fault

Name: VM_SENSOR_OUT_OF_TOLERANCE
Message: VM sensor reading outside +/-5% of nominal.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Rail regulation out of tolerance | VM sensor fault on the module

Name: RAIL_ADJUST_READBACK_MISMATCH
Message: Voltage rail adjustment not reflected in the VM readback.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Rail control path fault | VRM not applying the requested setpoint

Name: VMIN_ABOVE_RATED_LIMIT
Message: Vmin above the rated limit for an SA/SAU rail.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal silicon requiring higher voltage than rated | Rail delivery drop under load

Name: UNEXPECTED_DVFS_RAMPDOWN
Message: Unexpected DVFS rampdown event during a workload.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Power or thermal excursion triggering DVFS | Marginal rail under workload transients

Name: MODULE_POWER_ON_FAILURE
Message: Module failed to power on (indicators off, rail fault or short).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Verify that the green power indicators on the Sohu module are ON. Verify that both the PCIe cable and power cable are connected correctly and securely. If there is no trouble found, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Rail short (observed: VOUT_13P5_IBC, VDD_1P2) | VRM stuck below regulation (observed: VCC_VRM at 0.7V) | Devkit cannot communicate with the Sohu module, it is likely that the bootloader is not running because the PV1 is not powering on

Name: CHIP_ID_READ_OR_MISMATCH
Message: The sohu_chip_id sysfs attribute of an enumerated Sohu endpoint could not be read or parsed, read back as all ones (device in reset), or reported a chip ID other than the one the resource configuration expects for that PCIe location.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Sohu ASIC held in reset or dropped off the PCIe link mid-read | Wrong or unprogrammed chip ID strapping/efuse on the module | Module populated in a baseboard slot other than the one recorded in genealogy | Firmware failed to publish the chip ID to the sysfs attribute

Name: ASIC_RESET_DEASSERT_FAILED
Message: ASIC reset deassert failed.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: ASIC reset could not be deasserted

Name: SOHU_NOT_PINGABLE
Message: The Sohu device did not respond to a ping over the RPC proxy: the firmware is not running, not reachable, or the device dropped off the proxy. Emitted when a device that had been posting stops answering, for example the post-campaign sweep after a repeated-FLR run.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Sohu firmware hung or crashed and stopped servicing RPCs | Device dropped off the PCIe tree / vfio proxy | Marginal reset or power sequencing leaving the ASIC unresponsive

Name: PLDM_SENSOR_CHECK_FAILED
Message: PLDM sensor discoverability or sanity check failed (boot-phase gate).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Firmware PLDM stack not exposing sensors | Sensor fault on the module

Name: I2C_PERIPHERAL_READ_FAIL
Message: An I2C transaction on the Sohu mezzanine failed. This covers bring-up (initializing the ASIC-debug mux or any of the four Sohu I2C controllers, and reading the mezzanine board type) as well as the per-device probes on I2C0-I2C3, where a probe either failed its transaction or returned data that did not match the expected device identifier/register value. The first failure ends the test; for a probe it identifies the bus, device, and address.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Peripheral unpowered or not responding on the addressed bus | Wrong or unexpected device populated at the probed address | Open or marginal I2C trace / connector contact on the module | Sohu I2C controller fault | ASIC-debug I2C mux not responding, leaving no path to the mezzanine buses
Bugs: ETCH-35872: Chips not enumerated by RPC proxy

Name: GPIO_LOOPBACK_MISMATCH
Message: An MCPU GPIO did not read back its driven value. Covers both halves of the test: the chip-ID strap pins reading a value other than the expected chip_id, and the per-pin output->input loopback failing to observe either the flipped value or the restored original.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Open, shorted, or marginal GPIO net on the module | MCPU GPIO pad or pin-mux fault | Chip-ID strap resistors incorrect or not populated for this module

Name: UART_PING_LOG_MISMATCH
Message: UART ping log message absent or content mismatch.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: UART path fault on the module | Firmware boot log not produced

Name: JTAG_READBACK_MISMATCH
Message: A JTAG check did not produce the expected value, or could not be read at all: an ARC core cluster_id, the SA row/column build configuration, or a failure to select a core or read a register over the chain. The core1_cpu_reset read is recorded as a diagnostic measurement only and never fails the test. Failures before any JTAG transaction take the harness codes instead — an unknown jtag_interface is TH-HAR-0002, and no adapter matching serial_prefix or a missing OpenOCD binary are TH-HAR-0003.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal or defective ARC core / SA fabric on the ASIC | JTAG chain integrity problem on the module

Name: EFUSE_REGION_READ_FAILURE
Message: Reading the eFuse region over RPC failed, so no init config could be decoded from the module.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Defective eFuse macro or sense path on the module | eFuse region never programmed at OSAT (blank or corrupt map) | Sohu RPC link to the module dropped mid-read

Name: EFUSE_WS_FT_STATUS_INCOMPLETE
Message: The eFuse read succeeded but a wafer-sort or final-test completion flag (wafer_sort_complete, final_test_complete, mbist_complete, sa_complete, sensor_complete or hbm_complete) is False, so the module carries no record of a completed WS/FT flow including MBIST and SA repair.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Module skipped or aborted part of the WS/FT flow at the OSAT | MBIST or SA repair did not complete before the summary was burnt | Wrong or partially programmed eFuse map version for this build

Name: BUS_CONNECTIVITY_CSR_ACCESS_FAIL
Message: The mCPU-resident bus connectivity sweep reported a non-zero failed count: at least one CSR check across the SoC blocks (MCPU, ISC, IPU, CSRAM, WCU, GPIO, PAD, sensors hub, PCIe, SAMU, datalink, MACs) did not pass. A check fails either because a write/verify/restore readback did not return the written pattern, or because a read-only field did not hold its expected value.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Defective CSR block or unreachable register slave on the internal bus | Clock or reset not released for the affected block | Wrong firmware image or chip variant for the DUT (build-config field mismatch)

Name: SRAM_TEST_FAIL
Message: On-chip SRAM test failure (stuck bits / readback mismatch) - the RPC read/write/invert checks reported failing SRAM regions, or the March C+ binary exited non-zero. Failing SRAM names go in the message / affected_instances, never into new codes (spec §1.2). Note - a non-zero March C+ exit is not yet distinguishable from a launch error; refine when the binary exposes an exit-status contract.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Defective on-die SRAM cells (stuck bits) in ISC/NLU/theta/softmax SRAMs | Marginal SRAM timing under nominal voltage/frequency

Name: SA_MATMUL_NUMERIC_MISMATCH
Message: An SA matmul dispatcher test binary exited non-zero: systolic-array outputs did not match the funcsim reference. sa_sort screening tolerates a bounded number of defective SA columns, so a non-zero exit means the mismatches went beyond what the health map is allowed to mask out.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Defective systolic-array column(s) or DPU row producing wrong products | Marginal voltage or clock for the SA zones at the densities under test | HBM weight delivery fault feeding the SA (whole DPU row wiped out)

Name: ATTENTION_SAU_NUMERIC_MISMATCH
Message: An attention/SAU dispatcher test binary exited non-zero: one or more attention, KV-flush or SAU operations did not match the funcsim reference.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Defective SAU macro (PPU / WSSA / SCSA / softmax) producing wrong results | KV cache read/write path fault | Marginal voltage or clock for the SAU zones under test

Name: WORKLOAD_HANG_OPERATION_TIMEOUT
Message: Workload hang / operation timeout.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: SOHU workload or operation did not complete within its timeout

Name: WEIGHT_LOAD_SPOT_CHECK_MISMATCH
Message: Weight-load spot check failed: HBM-resident weights did not match the on-disk model after load (weight_load_test_app non-zero exit).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: HBM write/read path corrupting weights | DMA addressing fault | Incomplete or corrupted weight transfer into HBM

Name: INFERENCE_DISPATCH_TIME_ABOVE_LIMIT
Message: Sustained inference throughput on the million-token test did not reach the expected chip tokens/s (95% of the suite's expected_chip_tokens_per_second). Not wired yet: the check runs inside llama_mtt_app and the harness only sees the exit status, so a non-zero exit cannot be told apart from a model-creation or dataset failure. Emitting it needs the binary to signal the threshold failure distinctly, or the harness to parse MTT_results/metrics.txt.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Chip sustaining a lower clock than expected under continuous load | Thermal or power throttling during the run | Marginal SA/HBM path reducing effective inference rate

Name: END_TO_END_INFERENCE_NUMERIC_MISMATCH
Message: End-to-end inference numeric mismatch vs reference.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: SOHU inference output did not match the expected reference

Name: FLR_FAILED
Message: A Function Level Reset cycle did not complete cleanly: the reset request failed or went unanswered within flr_timeout_s (default 5.0s), or the device did not become available and pingable again within recovery_timeout_s (default 10.0s). Reported for the first failing iteration of the FLR campaign; per-iteration round-trip times are recorded as flr_round_trip_* measurements and are not compared against a limit.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Sohu firmware not re-initialising cleanly after FLR | PCIe link failing to retrain within the recovery window | Marginal reset or power sequencing on the module

Name: SAU_PLL_CONFIG_FAIL
Message: SAU/SA PLL configuration failure - firmware did not report a safe SAU PLL phase alignment after FLR, or a requested PLL glitch frequency did not read back within 5% of the target before the readback timeout.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal SAU/SA PLL failing to lock to a safe phase | DVFS/PLL control path fault (glitch frequency not applied) | Firmware phase-finding did not run or reported failure (see ETCH-35301)

Name: DEFECTIVE_SA_COLUMNS_EXCEED_LIMIT
Message: Defective SA column count exceeds the screening limit. Retry is futile for a defect map.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Systolic-array columns defective beyond the screening allowance

Name: PD_CHAIN_READ_FAILURE
Message: Process detector (PD) chain read failure.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: PD chain access fault | Marginal PD macro

Name: CHIP_BIN_BELOW_THRESHOLD
Message: Chip bin below the acceptance threshold / failed the binning criteria (e.g. unbinnable SA column mask count, or illegal bin transition).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Silicon performance below the acceptance bin | More masked SA columns than the supported binning limit

Name: SCREENING_DATA_MISSING
Message: Required screening data missing or failed to load (SA mask / bin inputs), including eFuse/Flash init-config read failures and invalid screening bin encodings.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Screening data package missing from the station or suite config | SA mask / bin inputs failed to parse | eFuse or Flash init config unreadable or inconsistent

Name: CHIP_STATE_SNAPSHOT_FAILED
Message: Chip state snapshot capture failed.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Chip not responding to the snapshot request | Snapshot tooling fault

Name: PLL_GLITCH_FREQUENCY_READBACK_FAILED
Message: RETIRED (ETCH-38346): historically emitted when PLL glitch frequency did not read back within 5% of the target before the timeout. New emissions use TH-SOHU-0020 (SAU_PLL_CONFIG_FAIL).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: PLL not locking at the requested glitch frequency | DVFS control path fault

Name: VFIO_PING_LATENCY_OUT_OF_SPEC
Message: VFIO ping responses were received but none met the allowed latency - the device is pingable but its response latency is out of spec. Distinct from TH-SOHU-0002 (no response at all).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Marginal PCIe link or device response path adding latency | Device under unexpected load or in a degraded state

Name: THERMAL_READING_OUT_OF_RANGE
Message: Thermal diode temperature reading out of the qualified range, reported invalid by the sensor, or an uncalibrated mezzanine diode reading below 0 C (bad solder joint indicator). Failing channels go in the message / affected_instances, never into new codes (spec §1.2).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Inspect the IBC TIM and ensure that the Sohu module is properly seated and secured in the fixture. Also verify that the Sohu module top cold plate is connected to the HRM cooling loop. If there is no trouble found, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Thermal forcing head not seated / poor contact | Bad solder joint on an uncalibrated mezzanine diode channel | Faulty TMP464 sensor or ASIC remote diode | Station ambient out of spec
Bugs: ETCH-35857: MLT DTS faiure Peak-to-peak deviation: 33029224 uC is out of bounds (30000000)

Name: DTS_SENSOR_VARIATION_EXCEEDED
Message: The peak-to-peak spread across the usable Sohu DTS readings exceeded the configured deviation limit (20C at L10). Zeroed and faulted sensors are excluded from the spread, so this reflects real sensor-to-sensor variation.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Inspect the IBC TIM and ensure that the Sohu module is properly seated and secured in the fixture. Also verify that the Sohu module top cold plate is connected to the HRM cooling loop. If there is no trouble found, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Uneven thermal forcing head seating across the die | TIM voids or uneven bond line | Defective DTS sensor reading high or low while still reporting no fault
Bugs: ETCH-35857: MLT DTS faiure Peak-to-peak deviation: 33029224 uC is out of bounds (30000000)

Name: CTS_PROTECTION_NO_SHUTDOWN
Message: The CTS trim code was driven to its maximum (lowest trip threshold) but the chip did not shut down: the CPLD cattrip latch bit in ASIC_CTRL1 was never set within the shutdown timeout.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Defective catastrophic trip sensor on the die (never asserts CATTRIP) | CATTRIP output pin or its mezzanine card trace open | CATTRIP masked on the mezzanine card CPLD (mcu_cattrip_mask misconfigured)

Name: CATASTROPHIC_TRIP_DURING_STRESS
Message: Catastrophic trip event during a stress workload.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Inspect the IBC TIM and ensure that the Sohu module is properly seated and secured in the fixture. Also verify that the Sohu module top cold plate is connected to the HRM cooling loop. If there is no trouble found, retest once.
Possible Root Cause: Thermal excursion under power virus | TIM or cold-plate contact degradation

Name: DTS_PTP_DEVIATION_OUT_OF_BOUNDS
Message: DTS peak-to-peak deviation under power virus out of bounds (threshold under review; bounds may be raised).
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: If any temperature reading is out of spec verify that the affected unit has completed the required 45-min TIM baking process. Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: TIM or thermal head contact variation | Threshold still under review | The TIM baking duration has been updated from 15 to 45 mins.
Bugs: ETCH-35857: MLT DTS faiure Peak-to-peak deviation: 33029224 uC is out of bounds (30000000)

Name: DTS_PEAK_TEMPERATURE_EXCEEDS_MAX
Message: Peak DTS temperature under power virus exceeds the expected maximum.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: If any temperature reading is out of spec verify that the affected unit has completed the required 45-min TIM baking process. Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: Unit did not complete the required 45-minute TIM baking process | TIM or cold-plate contact degradation | The TIM baking duration has been updated from 15 to 45 mins.

Name: THERMAL_TELEMETRY_UNAVAILABLE
Message: The TMP464 thermal diode data could not be obtained - RPC/connection failure over the VBB UART, or a malformed response (missing temperature array, unexpected channel count). The thermal verdict is inconclusive.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: Collect the suite/test logs and artifacts for this failure. Escalate to Etched engineer with the collected logs.
Possible Root Cause: VBB UART/RPC communication failure (shared bench UART contention) | VBB or sensor firmware fault returning malformed TMP464 data

Name: CPLD_CATTRIP_DETECTED
Message: The mezzanine CPLD reports a cattrip: the MCU cattrip latch is set, MCU cattrip is live with VCC_1V2 good, or an HBM cattrip channel is active. Emitted by CpldDiagnosticsTestCase when run with fail_on_cattrip, so the verdict names the thermal event instead of the workload that died under it.
Recover / Troubleshooting Procedure: If every slotted chip tripped, stop and check the station cooling (CDU status, coolant flow, HRM loop) before any retest. For a single chip, inspect the IBC TIM and reseat the module in the fixture; confirm the top cold plate is on the HRM loop. Escalate to Etched engineer with the CPLD reports and collector data.
Possible Root Cause: Station cooling fault (CDU, coolant flow, HRM loop) when every slotted chip trips together | TIM or cold-plate contact degradation on one module | Thermal excursion under a stress workload
